summary: Toru Kumoi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and at the Humanities Information Studies Institute, where he was attested as senior researcher in 2015.

Toru Sagara (1921–2000) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944) under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1942–1944). He held posts at Ibaraki University (~1950–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. Active in sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, he served at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, he held posts at Lausanne, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Toyo University from around 1966 to 1976. He later held a post at Toyo University from circa 1979 to 2018.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (-1982) under Karl Hoffmann and others. He held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003–2005).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Keio University (1931–1937), he taught there from 1937 to 1981, and later held positions at McGill University and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy.

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He later served at Tohoku University, as an associate professor at Tokai Gakuin University (~1978–1988), and at International Buddhist University (~2006).
Toshihiro Wada is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from circa 1989 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (-1995), he later held a professorship at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Toshikazu Watanabe works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2015–2019), and Kokugakuin University (2018).

Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1974–1982). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1993–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

Toshinori Ochiai works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (attested 2001), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2005), and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (attested 2020).
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Otani University and Doho University.

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo. He held research posts at Toyo University (attested 2015–2020) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning his degrees at Kyoto University. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1949–1968) and president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).
Toshio Sako is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University, working under teachers Yasunori Ejima, Jikido Takasaki, and Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Hannan University, the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977), and Chuo University (~1977–1987).
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Legal School, and Chuo University. He taught at Shakitoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa University, Toyo University, and Nihon University.
